hood_landmark.Kreuzberg: Checkpoint Charlie and the canal-side Bergmannkiez
hood_landmark.Mitte: The Brandenburg Gate and Museum Island
hood_landmark.Prenzlauer Berg: Mauerpark's Sunday flea market and open-air karaoke

avoid.reason: Generally safe; pickpocketing at Alexanderplatz and on the U-/S-Bahn; open drug dealing in Görlitzer Park and around Kottbusser Tor — caution at night

hood_desc: Kreuzberg is Berlin's multicultural, alternative core with legendary nightlife, Turkish markets, street art and canal-side bars, perfect for nightlife lovers and creatives.
Mitte is the historic and cultural center holding Museum Island, Brandenburg Gate and upscale galleries, ideal for first-time visitors and sightseers wanting central access.
Prenzlauer Berg is a beautifully restored, family-friendly district of cafes, playgrounds and Sunday markets, suited to families and travelers seeking a calmer stay.
Friedrichshain is a young, energetic area famed for techno clubs, the East Side Gallery and cheap eats, drawing partygoers and budget-minded backpackers.
Neukölln is Berlin's edgy, rapidly gentrifying hipster quarter with dive bars, diverse food and a raw creative energy, appealing to trend-seeking young travelers.

water.note: Tap water is strictly regulated and safe to drink.

transit.pay: There are no tap-in gates: buy tickets in the BVG Fahrinfo or S-Bahn app, or from station machines (cards accepted), and validate paper tickets before boarding. A zone AB single costs about 4 EUR (~US$4.50) and a day ticket about 11 EUR; one ticket covers U-Bahn, S-Bahn, trams and buses. Staying weeks? The Deutschland-Ticket (63 EUR/month) covers local transit nationwide.
transit.hours: U-Bahn and S-Bahn run roughly 4am-1am on weekdays and all night on Friday-Saturday nights; night buses cover the gaps midweek.

landmarks: Brandenburg Gate (Brandenburger Tor)
Berlin's premier neoclassical monument and symbol of German reunification.
Reichstag Building
The historic parliament building topped by Norman Foster's glass dome, offering panoramic city views.
Berlin TV Tower (Fernsehturm)
The tallest structure in Germany, an unmistakable sphere-topped spire dominating the skyline.
East Side Gallery
The longest remaining stretch of the Berlin Wall, covered in vibrant political murals.
Checkpoint Charlie
The famous Cold War border crossing between East and West Berlin, rich in history.
Berlin Cathedral (Berliner Dom)
A grand baroque cathedral on Museum Island with an iconic dome overlooking the Spree.
Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe
A somber, visually striking field of concrete stelae near the Brandenburg Gate.
Charlottenburg Palace
Berlin's largest palace, a baroque and rococo masterpiece with expansive gardens.
Victory Column (Siegessäule)
A gilded angel statue atop a column in the Tiergarten, one of Berlin's most photographed monuments.
Museum Island (Museumsinsel)
A UNESCO World Heritage complex of five major museums on an island in the Spree River.

train.note: Trains leave from Berlin Hauptbahnhof, though many international services also call at Berlin Ostbahnhof or Sudkreuz - check which one your ticket shows. Night options: an OeBB Nightjet also runs Berlin-Prague-Vienna/Budapest (seated cars), the Zurich Nightjet runs south via Leipzig, and European Sleeper now runs Paris-Berlin plus a Brussels-Amsterdam-Berlin-Prague train on selected nights. The old direct Paris and Vienna Nightjets run by OeBB were withdrawn in December 2025, so European Sleeper is the surviving overnight link to France. Booking for cross-border trains normally opens about six months ahead and the cheapest Sparpreis Europa fares go quickly.

intl.to: Poland, Czechia, Netherlands, France & across Europe

bus.note: International coaches use the ZOB (Zentraler Omnibusbahnhof) by the Funkturm in western Berlin, a staffed terminal reached by U-Bahn Kaiserdamm or S-Bahn Messe Nord. FlixBus dominates the European network; RegioJet is a good option toward Prague, taking around 4h30. Prague, Warsaw and Copenhagen are all doable in a day by coach, and tickets are cheapest booked online well in advance.

ferry.note: Berlin is inland, so there are no sea ferries - only sightseeing boats on the Spree and local lakes. For Baltic crossings to Scandinavia you would travel first to a coastal port such as Rostock or Sassnitz.
